- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer to lower end of forecast range.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially after 1–2 bullish sentiment spikes — leading to overshoot; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: model often fails to correct from recent highs/lows; adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 7–14 days.
- Forecasts with high sentiment volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00) show persistent bias toward overestimating volatility — reduce forecast variance or apply sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- For horizon > 14d, model tends to overestimate price movement; apply decay factor or reduce slope of trend component.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.33 or below) in last 3–5 days, model often fails to recognize reversal — adjust forecast downward with increasing confidence.
